item.title: Strait of Hormuz weekly transits hit highest since war began
item.description: The seven-day rolling average for vessel transits through the Strait of Hormuz has reached its highest point since the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran began on February 28, according to Bloomberg's Hormuz Tracker published Friday. A total of 13 ships crossed the strait since Friday morning, with 10 exiting the Persian Gulf and three entering, Bloomberg reported, citing vessel-tracking data. The uptick included ships with no apparent direct ties to Iran or China, as more countries negotiate passage rights with Tehran.

item.title: Iranian missile heavily damages Israeli drone factory
item.description:
An Iranian ballistic missile struck the production facility of AeroSentinel, a boutique Israeli drone manufacturer based in Petah Tikva, late Thursday night, leaving heavy structural damage at the site and raising questions about the impact on Israel's tactical drone supply during the ongoing war with Iran.

The 400-kilogram missile landed mere meters from the facility, according to The Jerusalem Post, which first reported the extent of the damage. No major casualties were reported, though footage from the scene showed a large crater and destroyed buildings. Emergency crews responded quickly, and the company said its team worked through the night to preserve "critical knowledge, capabilities, and core operational assets."

item.title: Petronas says shipping, insurance costs compound oil surge
item.description:
The effective blockade of the Strait of Hormuz has sent crude oil prices surging to their highest levels in nearly four years, with Brent crude peaking at $126 per barrel and trading around $112 as of April 3, reshaping global energy markets and inflicting cascading costs across international shipping and insurance.

Petronas CEO Tengku Muhammad Taufik said this week that the oil price surge — roughly 40% since the U.S.-Israel military campaign against Iran began on February 28 — is "not purely driven by supply and demand." Transportation costs have risen between 47% and 176%, while insurance premiums have surged up to 337%, according to the Malaysian state energy firm's chief. "Ship owners providing crude oil transportation services must take on risks. Insurance premiums also rise due to passing through conflict zones," Tengku Muhammad Taufik told reporters.

item.title: India confirms Iranian oil purchases amid Hormuz crisis
item.description: Oil prices have surged past $110 per barrel as the five-week-old blockade of the Strait of Hormuz — through which roughly 20% of the world's oil flows — continues to choke global energy supplies, with fresh airstrikes on Isfahan and a reported ship attack further elevating risk on the first weekend of April.

item.title: UN delays vote on Hormuz shipping resolution as Gulf states seek bypass routes
item.description: More than five weeks after joint U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran triggered the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, major Gulf oil producers are accelerating efforts to bypass the waterway that normally carries roughly one-fifth of the world's oil supply. The push for alternative export infrastructure comes as fuel shortages ripple across import-dependent nations and a diplomatic stalemate at the United Nations delays international action.

item.title: Iran rapidly repairing bombed missile sites, U.S. intel says
item.description: More than five weeks into the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran, a widening gap has emerged between President Trump's declarations of near-victory and the assessments of his own intelligence agencies, which paint a picture of an adversary that remains far more capable than the White House has acknowledged.

item.title: Israel hits Beirut, Tyre as Lebanon war enters second month
item.description: Israel broadened its aerial bombardment across Lebanon on Saturday, launching predawn strikes on Beirut's southern suburbs and renewing attacks on the coastal city of Tyre after issuing forced evacuation orders for its residents, as the war with Hezbollah entered its second month with no sign of abating.

item.title: Ukrainian drone strikes kill one in Taganrog, hit chemical plants deep in Russia
item.description:
A wave of Ukrainian drone and missile attacks struck southern Russia early Saturday, killing at least one person and seriously wounding four others in the port city of Taganrog, while a separate drone raid targeted chemical plants deep inside Russian territory in the city of Tolyatti.

Rostov region governor Yuri Slyusar said the attack on Taganrog left one dead and four in critical condition, including a foreign citizen. Commercial infrastructure was damaged and a fire broke out at the warehouses of a logistics company, he wrote on Telegram.

item.title: Debris from intercepted drones hits buildings across Dubai
item.description: Debris from an intercepted Iranian drone struck the facade of Oracle's building in Dubai Internet City early Saturday, as the Gulf conflict entered its fifth week with no sign of abating. The Dubai Media Office confirmed the incident in a post on X, calling it a "minor incident" and saying no injuries were reported.

item.title: US Embassy urges Americans to leave Lebanon over Iran university threats
item.description:
The U.S. Embassy in Beirut issued an urgent security alert on Friday urging all American citizens to depart Lebanon while commercial flights remain available, warning that Iran and its allied militias "may intend to target universities in Lebanon."

The advisory described the security environment as "volatile and unpredictable," citing ongoing airstrikes, drone activity, and rocket fire across the country, particularly in southern Lebanon, the Beqaa region, and parts of Beirut. "Iran has specifically threatened American universities across the Middle East," the embassy said, though it did not identify any specific institutions at risk.

item.title: Iran exempts Iraq from Strait of Hormuz restrictions
item.description:
Iran's unified military command announced Saturday that Iraq would be exempt from any restrictions imposed on the Strait of Hormuz, a move that could offer a lifeline to Baghdad's devastated oil economy after more than five weeks of conflict.

The Iraqi News Agency reported that the Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters — Iran's joint military command overseeing operations during the war — declared that "brotherly Iraq" would not be subject to the transit controls Tehran has enforced on the strategic waterway since late February. The announcement came as Iran simultaneously authorized the passage of vessels carrying essential and humanitarian goods to Iranian ports through the strait, according to Iran's semi-official Tasnim News Agency.

item.title: Iran authorizes humanitarian ships through Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iran on Saturday authorized the passage of ships carrying humanitarian and essential goods through the Strait of Hormuz, more than five weeks after its effective blockade of the critical waterway triggered a global energy crisis. The directive, reported by Iran's semi-official Tasnim News Agency, permits vessels carrying essential goods and livestock feed to transit under designated protocols coordinated with Iranian authorities.

item.title: Jordan says it downed 261 of 281 Iranian projectiles over five weeks
item.description: Jordan's armed forces announced Saturday that its air defenses intercepted and destroyed 261 out of 281 Iranian missiles and drones launched at the kingdom since the start of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, with 20 projectiles evading interception. The military said the 281 projectiles included 161 missiles and 120 drones that targeted "vital sites and facilities" within Jordanian territory.

item.title: Iran exempts Iraq from Hormuz restrictions as passage policy expands
item.description:
Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya joint military command announced on Saturday that Iraq would be exempt from any restrictions imposed on the Strait of Hormuz, according to Al Jazeera. The declaration by spokesperson Ebrahim Zolfaghari came as the war between Iran and the United States and Israel entered its 36th day, with Tehran continuing to leverage the critical waterway as its most potent strategic tool.

The move formalizes Iraq's status among a growing list of nations granted passage through the strait, which normally carries roughly a fifth of the world's oil trade. Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi had previously stated in late March, "We permitted passage through the Strait of Hormuz for friendly nations including China, Russia, India, Iraq, and Pakistan". Since then, the Philippines, Malaysia, Egypt, and South Korea have also reportedly secured passage rights.

item.title: Displaced Lebanese Shiites face sectarian hostility amid war
item.description: More than a month into the renewed war between Israel and Hezbollah, over 1.1 million displaced Lebanese — the vast majority of them Shiite Muslims — are confronting not only the devastation of airstrikes but a wave of sectarian hostility that has left many sleeping in tents, on streets, and in vehicles rather than seeking shelter in communities where they feel unwelcome.

item.title: Iran restoring bombed missile bunkers within hours, US intelligence finds
item.description: Iranian military personnel have been excavating bombed underground missile bunkers and silos, returning them to operational status within hours of being struck by American and Israeli forces, according to U.S. intelligence reports first disclosed by The New York Times on April 3. The findings cast fresh doubt on the Trump administration's claims that its five-week air campaign has brought Iran's ballistic missile capabilities to the brink of elimination.

item.title: Erdogan tells NATO chief Iran war has caused 'geostrategic impasse'
item.description:
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan told NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte on Saturday that the war involving Iran has led to a "geostrategic impasse," urging the international community to redouble diplomatic efforts to end the conflict, according to a statement from the Turkish presidency.

In the phone call, Erdogan said "the process started by the intervention against Iran" had created the deadlock and called for intensified international action, Anadolu Agency reported. He also praised NATO's support for Turkey's air defense during the crisis, saying it demonstrated the alliance's deterrence capability and solidarity.

item.title: Trump gives Iran 48 hours as strikes hit petrochemical sites
item.description: Israel has prepared a package of targets focused on Iran's energy facilities and critical infrastructure, with any strike now dependent on a decision by President Donald Trump, whose April 6 deadline for Tehran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz is days away. The development came as U.S. and Israeli forces struck key petrochemical facilities in southwestern Iran on Saturday and Trump issued a fresh 48-hour warning to Tehran.

item.title: Slovak, Hungarian PMs demand EU lift Russia energy sanctions
item.description: Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico on Saturday called on the European Union to immediately lift sanctions on Russian oil and gas imports, restore flows through the Druzhba pipeline, and end the conflict in Ukraine to address the deepening energy crisis triggered by the war in Iran. The demand came after a phone call with Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, who issued his own warning that Europe faces a mounting energy emergency.

item.title: Iran strikes Ben Gurion Airport, Gulf states with fresh drone and missile barrages
item.description: Iran's military announced Saturday that it carried out a large-scale drone attack on Israel's Ben Gurion Airport, striking several key facilities in what Tehran described as retaliation for continued American and Israeli military operations against Iranian territory. The strikes came as Gulf states absorbed yet another day of heavy aerial bombardment, and a drone hit one of the world's largest oil fields in southern Iraq.
